title: Next Greater Numerically Balanced Number
statement: Call an integer `x` numerically balanced when every digit `d` that appears in `x` appears exactly `d` times in it (so a balanced number never contains the digit 0). Given an integer `n`, return the smallest numerically balanced integer that is strictly larger than `n`.
notes:
## Intuition

Balanced numbers are rare but not far apart for small inputs: for every `n` up to 10^6 the answer is at most `1224444` (one 1, two 2s, four 4s). So the simplest correct plan works: try `n + 1`, `n + 2`, ... and test each candidate by counting its digits. The test is pure frequency counting: tally each digit, then every digit that occurs must occur exactly as many times as its value.

## Approach

1. Write `isBalanced(x)`: peel off digits with `x % 10` and `Math.floor(x / 10)`, adding one to `count[digit]` for each.
2. Then check every `digit` from 0 to 9: if it occurs (`count[digit] > 0`) but not exactly `digit` times, `x` is not balanced. A 0 always fails here, since it occurs but 0 times is required.
3. Start `candidate` at `n + 1` and increase it until `isBalanced(candidate)` holds; return it.

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 1`, so `candidate` starts at 2. The number 2 has `count[2] = 1`, not 2, so it fails; 3 to 9 fail the same way. 11 has `count[1] = 2` instead of 1; 20 and 21 fail on the 0 and the single 2. At 22, `count[2] = 2` and no other digit occurs, so the answer is `22`.

## Complexity

- Time: O((A - n) · log A), where A is the answer: each candidate costs one pass over its at most 7 digits. A is at most 1,224,444 under the constraints, so this is at most about 10^7 simple steps.
- Space: O(1): ten counters.

## Pitfalls

- The answer must be strictly greater than `n`, so start at `n + 1`; a balanced `n` is not its own answer.
- Any 0 digit makes a number unbalanced (1022 fails), which the `count[digit] > 0` check handles.
- The answer can exceed 10^6 (`n = 10^6` gives `1224444`), so do not cap the search at the input limit.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `isBalanced` | tests one number by counting its digits |
| `count` | how many times each digit 0 to 9 occurs in `x` |
| `digit` | the digit value being checked |
| `candidate` | the number currently being tried |

narration.2: A helper decides whether one number is balanced.
narration.3: Ten counters, one for each digit.
narration.4: Peel off the last digit until none are left.
narration.8: Check every digit value against its count.
narration.9: A digit that appears must appear exactly as many times as its value; 0 can never pass.
narration.10: One mismatch is enough to reject the number.
narration.13: Every present digit matched its count, so the number is balanced.
narration.15: The answer must be strictly greater than n, so start just above it.
narration.16: Keep moving up while the candidate is not balanced.
narration.19: The first balanced candidate is the smallest one above n.
